# 1 Enoch Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** And Enoch went and said: 'Azazel, you shall have no peace; a severe sentence has gone forth against you to put you in bonds.

**2** You shall have neither tolerance nor any petition granted to you, because of the unrighteousness you taught, and because of all the works of godlessness and unrighteousness and sin that you showed to men.'

**3** Then I went and spoke to them all together, and they were all afraid, and fear and trembling seized them.

**4** And they besought me to write a petition on their behalf, that they might find forgiveness, and to read their petition in the presence of the Lord of heaven.

**5** For from that time forward they could not speak with Him, nor raise their eyes to heaven, for shame of their sins for which they had been condemned.

**6** Then I wrote out their petition, and the prayer concerning their spirits and their deeds, each one individually, and concerning their requests that they should have forgiveness and length of days.

**7** And I went and sat down at the waters of Dan, in the land of Dan, to the south of the west of Hermon. I read their petition until I fell asleep.

**8** And behold, a dream came to me, and visions fell upon me, and I saw visions of wrath, and a voice came bidding me to tell the sons of heaven and to reprimand them.

**9** And when I awoke, I came to them; they were all sitting gathered together, weeping, in Abel-mayin, which is between Lebanon and Senir, with their faces covered.

**10** And I recounted before them all the visions I had seen in sleep, and I began to speak the words of righteousness and to reprimand the heavenly Watchers.

---

*LOGOS notes: Chapter 13 narrates Enoch's role as scribe-intercessor: he delivers the verdict to Azazel (vv. 1–2), is approached by all the Watchers for intercession (vv. 3–6), withdraws to the waters of Dan to read their petition and receive a vision (vv. 7–8), and returns to deliver the divine response (vv. 9–10). The location 'Abel-mayin' (= 'meadow of waters') connects to the geography of the Hermon tradition in ch. 6.*
